title: SKD Spec: Core Vision and Purpose
description:
The Structured Knowledge Document (SKD) is a document architecture that separates Objective Reality (what happened) from Subjective Reality (what it means). It emerged from work on the Knowledge Organization Framework (KOF) as the foundational protocol underlying that system.

Key insight: KOF was tightly coupling several concepts - the core epistemological protocol (SKD), the multi-perspective methodology, and the tooling. SKD is the pure foundation that other applications can build upon.

SKD is meant to be:
- A shareable standard others can adopt
- Human consumable (designed for reading, not just machine processing)
- Independent of any specific tooling or methodology
- The author's (Don Schartman) creation with attribution preserved

The spec defines 4 invariant chambers: Definitions, Objective Observations, Logic Chain, Subjective Interpretations. These never change regardless of application.

Related repo: knowledge-organization-framework (an application of SKD)

title: Decide on licensing model
description:
The SKD is meant to be shareable but also 'special' - the author wants recognition and some form of ownership/credit.

Options to consider:
- Creative Commons with attribution (CC BY)
- MIT license (very permissive)
- Custom license with attribution requirements
- Dual licensing (open for personal, commercial requires license)

The value proposition: the concept is shareable, but tooling built on it (like KOF) is where differentiation happens. Similar to Markdown (open spec) → Obsidian (valuable app).
